PagerBot: scheduled-maint: Planned kernel security patching for serving-us-west1 cluster on 2026-03-20 02:00-04:00 UTC. Expected behaviour: rolling node evacuations, per-node drain ~60-120s, graceful fallback to warm replicas. Please ack if you are covering and confirm customer comms.

Aisha (oncall): acked. I'm oncall for that window — will follow the evacuation play. @Ben can you post the runbook snippet and rollback hook?

Ben (eng-infra): yup. runbook tldr: 
```
1. Preflight checks: cluster health, KV cache primaries, load heatmap.
2. Cordon node, trigger drain: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.
3. Observe p99 latency and request error rate for 10m after each drain.
4. If errors > 1% or p99 > 2500ms, stop roll and revert cordons, rejoin nodes.
5. After all nodes patched, uncordon and run smoke tests; push statuspage and customer comms.
```
If we need fast rollback, reimage to previous AMI and reattach.

Jill (sre): adding a note: watch KV cache warmup — some models have cold-kv spikes. Suggest we set temporary routing to lower-capacity variant for non-critical customers during drains. Also enable prefix caching for high-volume sessions.

Aisha (oncall): good call. I'll prep a brief statuspage draft and a short customer email template. Pls review.

Elena (support): posting customer-facing copy (short/concise): 

---
Short notice for customers (email + status page):
We will perform a planned maintenance in the us-west1 serving cluster on 2026-03-20 from 02:00–04:00 UTC to apply a security patch. During the window you may see brief, intermittent request retries or slightly elevated latency while nodes are drained and restarted. Most requests should succeed; if you see persistent errors, please reach out to support@redwood.ai with your request ID. We do not expect data loss.
---

Longer statuspage draft (more explicit):
We are applying an urgent kernel security update to servers in the us-west1 inference cluster. We will perform a rolling node evacuation to minimize customer impact. Expected effects: short retries (seconds) and brief latency spikes for ongoing sessions. Mitigations: automatic fallback to warm replicas, routing to compatible model variants, and extended logging for immediate triage. ETA for full completion: 04:00 UTC.

Marcus (product): can we add an opt-out note for dedicated/private customers who need to schedule with their rep? Also, include contact for SLA-sensitive customers.

Elena (support): added: "If you have reserved Dedicated capacity or an existing maintenance agreement, please contact your account rep to coordinate a bespoke window if this one is unacceptable." And: "For SLA-sensitive use, open a ticket and mark it URGENT."

Ben (eng-infra): ops checklist to paste into the announcement channel (internal): 
```
- [ ] Confirm patch binary verified on staging
- [ ] Snapshot control-plane config and relevant manifests
- [ ] Notify CDN and edge teams for routing adjustments
- [ ] Launch staggered cordons (zone by zone)
- [ ] Monitor telemetry: p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate, queue lengths
- [ ] Escalate to emergency rollback on threshold breaches
```

Aisha (oncall): I'm going to run a quick preflight at 01:30 UTC and post green/red here. If green, we let the window proceed. If red, we shift to the backup window and update statuspage.

PagerBot: paging Aisha (oncall) — you have an active maintenance ack.

01:31 Aisha (oncall): preflight green: control-plane healthy, KV cache primaries stable, smoke tests pass on staging. I'll start the first cordon at 02:05 UTC.

02:06 Aisha (oncall): cordoned node-14-uw1 and triggered drain. Observing tail traffic. p99 increased ~300ms for ~40s, no 5xx. continuing.

02:18 Jill (sre): node-14 back up on patched kernel. KV cache warmed in ~90s. No errors. :white_check_mark:

02:30 Ben (eng-infra): cordoned node-21. p99 spike ~400ms for 35s, 5xx <0.05%. Proceeding.

02:47 Aisha (oncall): noticed a short cluster-wide spike at 02:45 — intermittent 429s from rate limiter for a small subset of high-throughput keys. Rolled back temporary rate-limit tweak, traffic normalized. Documenting in postmortem notes.

02:50 Marcus (product): any customer reports?

02:52 Elena (support): two inbound tickets from small customers about retries; both auto-retried and work resumed. I replied with the statuspage blurb and asked for request IDs if they still see issues.

03:15 Ben (eng-infra): final node patching underway. All cordons complete, smoke tests running.

03:27 Aisha (oncall): uncordoning node-14 and running final end-to-end test. Verified token-level cost metrics stable.

03:40 Aisha (oncall): maintenance complete. No sustained errors or customer-impacting outages. Rolling status update to statuspage and sending customer completion email.

Elena (support): customer completion copy: 
"Maintenance complete: The scheduled kernel patch on us-west1 finished at 03:40 UTC. During the window you may have seen brief retries or latency spikes; there are no ongoing issues tied to this maintenance. If you continue to see errors, please open a ticket and include request IDs. Thank you for your patience."

Aisha (oncall): posting statuspage:
- status: resolved
- details: kernel patch complete; rolling drains and restarts finished; monitoring green
- timeline: 02:05 start cordon, 03:40 maintenance complete

Jill (sre): adding short internal note for post-ops: track KV cache cold-start patterns over next 24h, and surface any regressions to model-onboarding.

Ben (eng-infra): dropping the runbook snippet we used into the runbook repo after small edits.

Marcus (product): thanks all. Good coordination. We should reuse the customer wording template for next short notice.

Aisha (oncall): closing thread. If anyone wants to add to the postmortem, drop notes here in next 48h. :thumbsup:

PagerBot: maintenance-ops: completed action: mark-ops-window-3098765432 as finished.
